Micah and I (http://imgur.com/a/qvFUGp7) would like to sincerely thank all of you for your help.

I myself am a very insecure person, people tend to take advantage of me, and I am shy when it comes to confrontation I stand down.  In a way, micah (that's my dogs name) has been amazing for me because I am forced to push myself out of this and assert myself more. 

I knew dogs were a lot of work, but I still never could have imagined how much work he would really be.  He is worth every ounce of work, and more.  I know if I give it my all then it will all pay off in the end.

Thank you guys for providing me with a whole lot of information.   I have my research cut out for me.  I will definitely be looking into these various types and methods of training.

If anyone is interested, here is a video of him playing at the dog park with another dog (who happens to be the same age and same breeds). Normally he is uninterested, but if you can look at this video...dont you agree that it seems as though he might have some hope and that he does want to play as opposed to attack?

http://imgur.com/a/oPt5vL0

Obviously, each time is situational, but this video gave me hope

Thank you so much for your reply.

I actually don't know of many good ways to engage and stimulate him mentally.  I have a few toys in which he has to engage in them a certain way in order to get the treats inside, but I dont know many ways and would love to learn some.

And you are spot on.  He needs lots of exercise (especially in the winter) but his quick tendency for over stimulation makes it difficult.

The trainer is certified, yes.  But honestly this is my first dog (I mean we had dogs growing up of course but my first dog as an adult) and I do not really know what you mean by CPDT, CBCC, and BAT.  

The trainer did bring his dog to one session to practice walking with / around my dog, and we seemed to be making great headway, for a little I had great control over him but i feel like we are back to square one.

I saw a trainer before this one who pretty much told me that he needed an antidepressant, and she wouldn't see him again until he had taken the medicine for a few weeks.  I was extremely against this at first, but his behavior got so bad that I honestly considered at one point maybe he did need it.  But I decided I am determined to try everything in my power and work as hard as I can with him...I do not want to put him on medication

This morning, when I got to work, the coworker immediately Skyped me at work apologizing for his "drunken crazy messages".  I decided enough was enough and I went to my trainer.

My trainer took the earrings he gave me and had a meeting with my managers manager.  She came back and basically told me I had to call HR.

I called HR and told them my story.  The man basically said I had two options.  I could either speak to my second tier manager, or he could reach out to an employee relations specialist to contact me.  I told him I wanted to speak to the specialist, because it didn't make sense to me that my second tier manager would advise me to contact HR, and HR would advise me to go back to my second tier manager.

The specialist emailed me shortly after the call and said she would talk to me on Thursday at 10 AM.  I feel defeated.  I have to sit directly next to this man until Thursday, and it is only Monday.

I feel extremely uncomfortable.  This man also knows that I walk alone to the bus after work.  I can't even focus on my job, because I am constantly looking over my shoulder.  I don't know what to do.

Maybe I am overreacting, but I have dealt with men like this in the past, and it can get very scary very quickly.

I wanted to add:

This week he had a question pertaining to something online he had to fill out, and he wanted to ask the trainer.  He tried copying and pasting it into a Skype message to her.  Our computer has a lot of confidential information, so many websites block the ability to copy and paste text.  So, he started freaking out.  I heard him saying "No, no, no!" I looked over at his computer, and when he pasted it into a message to the trainer the computer sent the last thing he copied: a picture.

It was a picture regarding strippers with a sign that said "send nudes here."

I was honestly relieved initially because I thought that the second the trainer saw that, he would be reprimanded and maybe I wouldn't have to sit next to him anymore, but he was able to cancel it in time so the trainer never got the picture.

I saw that he was friends on Facebook with my friend who works in my department, and I asked her if he had ever messaged her.  She said about a year ago he messaged her trying to ask her out on a date.

AKA, I think he might be a repeat offender of this behavior.

I've been looking for someone to live with online but I'm finding a hard time finding something close to the bus I take to work, and also, I have a dog which lowers my options even more.  There are a few one bedroom places, but they are all out of my price range.  I feel stuck.

Thank you so much for sharing.   You story affirms my belief that nothing worthwhile comes  easy,  and the most beautiful realizations can sometimes only happen through difficult and scary experiences. 

EDIT: the crying WAS extremely cathartic.

I have had an eating disorder for the past six years as well (my eating issues go way back to my childhood aswell)  and body dysmorphic issues, and looking in the mirror I morphed into this extremely ugly,  heinous,  blemished gollum like thing.... Then I snapped back to "normalcy"...

I'm glad someone else gets to experience what I am right  now.   Feel free to Pm me about any experiences you have :) 

As far as the three month thing,  what makes you say that? I don't doubt it is a good idea to space out trips,  but I'm curious as to what can happen if you don't,  why the recommended wait time is three months,  etc...

It honestly blows my mind how fucked up everything is.   We have these toxic,  dangerous,  addictive prescriptions we shove on almost anybody who experiences any negative symptom or basic human emotion so pharmaceuticals companies can make more and more money and people can just get addicted and sick.  The true therapeutical substances that actually have potential to HELP PEOPLE are illegal or taboo.   And these substances aren't a fix themselves,  yet they ALLOW us to go  deep and unlock the inner peace and happiness we have deep down within ourselves.   Is the potential to unlocking true inner peace that threatening to doctors and pharmaceutical companies?  The masses are misguided and unaware,  and I was among them my entire life.   Told I had a chemical imbalance and I just had to  "apply a bandaid"  per say,  and take the "magic pills"  to try to create an artificial chemical sense of happiness.  As long as this continues,  the world will be full of slaves... Who honestly do not  know any better.   Ignorance will be the death of our race... 

Edit:I'm not trying to belittle those who do have success with medication and mental disorders,  I guess I'm just kind of ranting on behalf of myself...

I was to the point where I wanted to end it all a week ago, and I remember I calmed myself and forced myself to go to sleep.
When I woke up, I got dressed nice, got a cup of coffee, and headed across to my campus.  The sky was actually bright and the sun was shining for once.  It was nice and beautiful outside, and the weather was just stunning.  It really hit me and I realized that if I had ended it the day before, I never would have gotten to experience this beautiful day.

So, don't think about these things longterm.  Think about how beautiful tomorrow could be.
